summary_en: This phase 1 trial studies the side effects of pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) in patients with ovarian, uterine, appendiceal, gastric, or colorectal cancer that has spread to the lining of the abdomen. PIPAC is given during a laparoscopic procedure using chemotherapy such as cisplatin, doxorubicin, oxaliplatin, or mitomycin, with some drugs also given by IV, and treatment repeats every 4 to 6 weeks for up to 3 cycles, or every 28 days in one group. The record states that the study looks at side effects and safety and efficacy, but the main outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 estudia los efectos secundarios de la quimioterapia en aerosol intraperitoneal presurizado (PIPAC) en pacientes con cáncer de ovario, uterino, de apéndice, gástrico o colorrectal que se ha diseminado al revestimiento de la cavidad abdominal. La PIPAC se administra durante un procedimiento laparoscópico con quimioterapia como cisplatino, doxorrubicina, oxaliplatino o mitomicina, y algunos medicamentos también se dan por vía intravenosa; el tratamiento se repite cada 4 a 6 semanas hasta 3 ciclos, o cada 28 días en un grupo. El registro indica que el estudio analiza los efectos secundarios, la seguridad y la eficacia, pero no se indica la medida de resultado principal.
who_for: Confirmed ovarian, uterine, gastric, appendiceal, or colorectal cancer with peritoneal carcinomatosis
ECOG performance status of 2 or less
Blood counts, liver, and kidney tests within the stated limits
Peritoneal disease visible on imaging or laparoscopy, with progression on prior chemotherapy (varies by group)
Not a candidate for cytoreduction and HIPEC; ascites 5 liters or less
not_for: Cancer spread outside the peritoneum (gastric, colorectal, or appendiceal groups)
Prior maximum cumulative doses of anthracycline drugs (ovarian, uterine, gastric group)
Known DPD deficiency (colorectal or appendiceal groups)
Bowel obstruction needing a feeding tube or total parenteral nutrition
Prior intra-abdominal aerosol chemotherapy, or pregnancy
